findings.text: follow-on: the count-equality assertions compare the audit's own traversal against a second traversal of the same loaded catalogue, so they cannot detect the failure the docstring names. audited_signal is the number of items _signal_rules yields -- 'for system in SYSTEMS: load_packaged_signal_map(MACHINE, system).signals' -- and declared_signal is 'sum(len(load_packaged_signal_map(MACHINE, system).signals) for system in SYSTEMS)': the identical expression over the identical SYSTEMS tuple, so the two sides drop together whenever a signal map loses rules and the assertion holds. The machine pair shares its loader too: _machine_bindings() calls load_packaged_machine_map(MACHINE), and declared_machine calls load_machine_map(bundle_for_machine(MACHINE).machine_map_path(MACHINE)); load_packaged_machine_map (packages/imas-alambic/src/imas-alambic... machine_map.py:1877-1883) returns exactly 'load_machine_map(bundle.machine_map_path(component))', so both arms read the same file through the same code path. The assertion can therefore only redden if the audit's own generator (_machine_bindings... _signal_rules) is edited to skip -- which is the one mutation the node's negative control applied -- not if a catalogue half fails to load or silently shrinks. The docstring's 'counted independently through the machine-map loader' overstates the independence.

follow-on: declared_machine re-implements, inline, the MachineMapCatalog.bound_channel_count property ('sum(len(bindings) for bindings in self.binding_sets.values())', machine_map.py:1300-1302) rather than calling it, so the catalogue's own declared total and the audit's copy of it can drift. Loading the catalogue once and reading .bound_channel_count would state the same comparison against the catalogue's public definition.
